leads.title: Civil Marriage Act - federal same-sex marriage law (2005)
leads.documents: Nationwide legalization of same-sex marriage, which closed the PEI exception; article notes PEI was among the 4 jurisdictions (with Alberta, Northwest Territories, Nunavut) not yet recognizing same-sex marriage as of July 2005 before Parliament acted.
leads.detail: Text states: 'Parliament passed the bill on July 20, 2005, making Canada the fourth country to legalize same-sex marriage nationwide.' No URL or footnote reference number visible in provided excerpt.

leads.title: Provincial court decisions on same-sex marriage 2002-2005 - PEI exclusion statement
leads.documents: Documents PEI legal status timeline: that by July 2005 same-sex marriages were legally recognized in all provinces/territories except Alberta, Prince Edward Island, Northwest Territories and Nunavut.
leads.detail: Direct quote: 'By July 2005, same-sex marriages were legally recognized in all provinces and territories except Alberta, Prince Edward Island, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut'. No URL or citation detail visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Prince Edward Island joint adoption legalization (2009)
leads.documents: Documents family-rights status in PEI: PEI legalized joint adoption by same-sex couples in 2009, after New Brunswick (2008) and before Nunavut (2011).
leads.detail: Direct quote: 'New Brunswick legalized joint adoption in 2008, while Prince Edward Island did so in 2009.' No URL or citation detail visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - Section 15(1) equality guarantee
leads.documents: Constitutional rights machinery applicable in PEI; supreme law basis for LGBTQ equality protection against discrimination by laws and government institutions including law enforcement.
leads.detail: Quoted in text as s.15(1) equality text starting 'Every individual is equal before and under the law...'. No URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Egan v. Canada (1995) - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is included in Section 15 as an analogous ground, granting equal protection - applicable to PEI as federal constitutional precedent.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'landmark decision in 1995, Egan v Canada' and 'Egan v. Canada, the Supreme Court... declared that sexual orientation was included within the bounds of section 15'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta (1998) - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Human-rights machinery precedent: failure of a provincial legislature to include sexual orientation in human rights law violates Section 15; basis for requirement noted as 'As of 2017, all provinces, territories, and the federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity'.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In its 1998 decision in Vriend v Alberta, the Supreme Court found...' No URL visible.

leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Federal decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity between consenting adults in private (in force June 27, 1969) - foundational criminal legality applying in PEI.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (also known as Bill C-150) was brought into force upon royal assent' and June 1969 passage. No URL visible.

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act (royal assent June 21, 2018)
leads.documents: Federal enforcement/remedy machinery: allows destruction/removal of judicial records for pre-1969 homosexual acts and former Criminal Code s.159 anal intercourse convictions by RCMP/federal departments and notification to provincial/municipal police/courts.
leads.detail: Cited with French title 'Loi sur la radiation de condamnations constituant des injustices historiques' and Parole Board distinction. No URL visible.
